nodes.summary: For a natural number $j$ let $M_j = 2^j - 1$ be the $j$-th Mersenne number (so $M_0 = 0$). For every natural number $t$ there are natural numbers $a$ and $d > 0$ such that, for every natural number $r$, every natural number $j \le t$ and every natural number $n$, the number $(a + rd + M_j) \cdot 2^n + 1$ is composite.
nodes.title: Composite numbers from Mersenne shifts of an arithmetic progression

nodes.summary: Let $b > 509203$ be a natural number. Then there are infinitely many Riesel numbers of the form $k(b^t - 1)/(b - 1)$ with $1 \le k < b$ and $t \ge 1$, that is, $b$-repdigits: the digit $k$ written $t$ times in base $b$.
nodes.title: Infinitely many Riesel repdigits in every base $b > 509203$

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a Riesel number that has Riesel covering data, so that $k$ is produced as a Riesel number by the covering system method. Then for every natural number $b \ge 2$ there are infinitely many $t \ge 1$ such that the $b$-repinteger $k_b^{(t)} = k\,(b^{\ell t} - 1)/(b^{\ell} - 1)$, where $\ell$ is the number of base-$b$ digits of $k$ (so $k_b^{(t)}$ is $k$ written $t$ times in base $b$), is a Riesel number.
nodes.title: Covering-produced Riesel numbers give infinitely many Riesel repintegers

nodes.summary: Let $b$ be a natural number with $b \equiv 16518444216571 \pmod{18446744073709551615}$, where $18446744073709551615 = 2^{64} - 1$. Then there are infinitely many Riesel numbers among the $b$-repunits $(b^t - 1)/(b - 1)$ with $t \ge 1$.

nodes.summary: Let $b$ and $t$ be natural numbers with $b \equiv 180 \pmod{11184810}$ and $t \equiv 171 \pmod{240}$. Then the $b$-repinteger $101_b^{(t)}$, which is the repdigit $101\,(b^t - 1)/(b - 1)$ because $101 < b$, is a Riesel number.

nodes.summary: For every natural number $t \equiv 31 \pmod{56}$, the binary repinteger $18107_2^{(t)} = 18107\,(2^{15t} - 1)/(2^{15} - 1)$, whose binary expansion is that of $18107$ (fifteen binary digits) written $t$ times, is a Riesel number.
nodes.title: Binary repintegers of 18107 that are Riesel numbers

nodes.summary: For every natural number $t$ with $t \equiv 1369 \pmod{2730}$ or $t \equiv 2599 \pmod{2730}$, the binary repstring $659_2^{(2;t)} = 659\,(2^{12t} - 1)/(2^{12} - 1)$ is a Riesel number. Its binary expansion is that of $659$ (ten binary digits) written $t$ times with two zeros between consecutive copies.
nodes.title: Binary repstrings of 659 that are Riesel numbers

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number and $S$ a finite set of triples $(r, m, p)$ of natural numbers. Then $S$ is Sierpiński covering data for $k$ if every integer is congruent to $r$ modulo $m$ for some $(r, m, p) \in S$, distinct triples in $S$ have distinct third entries, and every $(r, m, p) \in S$ has $m \ge 1$, $p$ prime, $p \mid 2^m - 1$ and $p \mid k \cdot 2^r + 1$.
nodes.title: Sierpiński covering data

nodes.summary: For every natural number $t \equiv 25 \pmod{56}$, the binary repinteger $18107_2^{(t)} = 18107\,(2^{15t} - 1)/(2^{15} - 1)$, whose binary expansion is that of $18107$ (fifteen binary digits) written $t$ times, is a Sierpiński number.
nodes.title: Binary repintegers of 18107 that are Sierpiński numbers

nodes.summary: Let $b$ and $t$ be natural numbers with $b \equiv 87 \pmod{11184810}$ and $t \equiv 59 \pmod{120}$. Then the base-$b$ repdigit $41_b^{(t)} = 41\,(b^t - 1)/(b - 1)$ is a Sierpiński number. Since $b \ge 87 > 41$, its $t$ base-$b$ digits all equal $41$.
nodes.title: Repdigits with digit 41 that are Sierpiński numbers

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$, $\mathfrak{t} \ge 1$, $w \ge 1$ and $z \ge 0$ be natural numbers. There is a single finite set of triples that is Sierpiński covering data for the $2$-repstring $k_2^{(z;t)}$ for every $t \ge 1$ with $t \equiv \mathfrak{t} \pmod{w}$ if and only if there is a single finite set of triples that is Riesel covering data for $k_2^{(z;t')}$ for every $t' \ge 1$ with $t' \equiv -\mathfrak{t} \pmod{w}$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
